# `bench` standard library

The `bench` module provides monotonic-clock microbenchmarking with warmup iterations
and formatted `ns/op` (or `us/op`, `ms/op`) throughput reporting.

```{.dva .run}
#use bench
#use io

r = bench::measure(100, i => i * i + 1)
io::out $ r.iters
```

## Types and Function catalog

| Symbol / Function | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `bench::BenchResult` | Record `(name: String, iters: Int, total_ns: Int, ns_per_op: Int)` | Benchmark timing result |
| `bench::measure_warmup(name, warmup, iters, fn)` | `String, Int, Int, (() => ()) => BenchResult` | Runs `warmup` unmeasured iterations, then times `iters` iterations of `fn` |
| `bench::measure(name, iters, fn)` | `String, Int, (() => ()) => BenchResult` | Measures `iters` iterations of `fn` with automatic 10% warmup |
| `bench::format_result(r)` | `BenchResult => String` | Formats result as `BENCH <name>: <iters> iters in <total> (<rate>/op)` |
| `bench::run(name, iters, fn)` | `String, Int, (() => ()) => BenchResult` | Measures `fn` and prints the formatted benchmark line to stdout |
| `bench::elapsed_ns(fn)` | `(() => ()) => Int` | Executes `fn` once and returns elapsed monotonic nanoseconds |
| `bench::elapsed_ms(fn)` | `(() => ()) => Float` | Executes `fn` once and returns elapsed monotonic milliseconds |
